papers.title: Is the learner or the summary the limit? Auditing machine-learning energy reconstruction for air-shower arrays on KASCADE and GRAPES-3
papers.abstract: Machine-learning energy estimators for cosmic-ray arrays are usually trained on a few fitted shower parameters, not station signals. When their resolution stops improving, standard diagnostics cannot say whether a better model would help or the summary has run out of information. We use a five-step audit that compares trained models with a learner-independent estimate of the lowest error the summary allows (its squared-loss Bayes risk, or floor), tests which inputs add information and flags inputs merely computed from the fit. We apply it to public KASCADE simulations with three hadronic-interaction models (QGSJET-II-04, EPOS-LHC and SIBYLL-2.3d), to 13,848,509 measured KASCADE events and to simulated GRAPES-3 events. Within known energy decades below 10^16 eV, gradient boosting on nine reconstructed features is within 2.2% of the estimated floor under every estimator setting, so more capacity is not expected to gain more than about 2%. The floor is an estimate, accurate to about 1% in a semi-synthetic benchmark with intervals that under-cover, and not a bound on the true Bayes risk. Replacing reconstructed by true particle numbers removes 70 to 72% of the error variance below 10^15 eV and 24 to 26% between 10^16 and 10^17 eV on all three models, yet simulated station signals close about a tenth of that gap. On GRAPES-3, networks given images rendered from the fit do no better than the fit. In measured data, the mean muon size at fixed electron size lies within every model's proton-to-iron bracket and a label-free probe finds the muon channel used as in simulation; neither fixes the energy scale. Energy-labelled results are simulated.

papers.title: Constraints on ultralight dark matter couplings from orbital perturbations of binary pulsars
papers.abstract: Ultralight dark matter coupled directly to ordinary matter perturbs the orbits of binary pulsars, and the perturbation grows secularly when its frequency matches a harmonic of the orbital motion. We use this effect to constrain three couplings with the wideband timing data for the $50$ binary pulsars of the NANOGrav 15 yr data set: a linear and a quadratic universal coupling of a scalar field to matter, and a vector field coupled to baryon minus lepton number ($B-L$). For every system and for masses between $10^{-23}$ and $10^{-18}\,$eV, we build the timing signature from the perturbed orbital elements. We then sample the coupling together with the local amplitude, phase and direction of the field and the red noise of the pulsar, marginalizing analytically over the timing model, and combine the single-pulsar likelihoods into $95\%$ credible upper limits at each mass. For a universal linear coupling, the orbital resonances of the eccentric systems bring the limit close to the Cassini bound. For the quadratic coupling, treating the neutron star as a point particle, the limits are the strongest available between $2\times10^{-22}$ and $2\times10^{-21}\,$eV. In the case of vector ultralight dark matter, the limit is comparable to the PPTA and E\"ot-Wash bounds between $3\times10^{-22}$ and $10^{-21}\,$eV and reaches or beats the E\"ot-Wash bound at isolated orbital resonances, while MICROSCOPE remains stronger over the entire mass range.

papers.title: Reliability of Fermi/GBM spectral-catalogue parameters for gamma-ray burst population studies
papers.abstract: The Fermi Gamma-ray Burst Monitor (GBM) spectral catalogue contains measurements affected by model uncertainties, different peak-flux (PFLX) integration times, and changes in catalogue processing. We examine which quantities describe spectral shape and which reflect brightness or measurement conditions. We analysed 3337 of 3378 GRBs with spectral-fit data and identified a catalogue transition at GRB180712358. We compared the two periods using rank-based tests, regressions, and catalogue model-selection rules, and assessed duration classification by repeated cross-validation. PFLX measurements at 64 and nominal 1024 ms were analysed separately; short-long comparisons used fluence (FLNC) measurements only. The transition coincides with changes in catalogue version, fit statistic, and fit fields. In the nominal 1024 ms sample, all ten COMP A-B rank-biserial effects have absolute values below 0.10. In the 64 ms sample, COMP shape parameters are similar, but amplitudes, fluxes, and fluences are higher in the later period. The origin of this difference is unknown. In the earlier period, brighter bursts have smaller parameter errors but larger reported fit statistics and stronger evidence for spectral curvature. The FLNC PLAW index measures broad-band hardness. BAND alpha and Epeak can describe spectral shape when their errors are controlled, but beta is often poorly constrained. Adding PLAW or BAND to COMP provides little additional duration-classification information in matched samples. We interpret the A-B division mainly as a catalogue-processing transition, not population evolution. Fit statistics, errors, metadata, and model labels describe measurement conditions and should not be treated as independent physical variables. Correlated model parameters should not be treated as independent.

papers.title: The Sensitivity of Gamma-Ray Searches for Dark Matter Annihilation in Milky Way Dwarf Galaxies: the LSST Era and Beyond
papers.abstract: We forecast the sensitivity of gamma-ray searches to dark matter annihilation in Milky Way satellite dwarf galaxies using BabyBison, a Monte Carlo pipeline combining cosmological satellite simulations and observational selection functions with a joint likelihood analysis of gamma-ray data. Although LSST is expected to substantially expand the catalog of known satellite galaxies, we find that these discoveries are likely to produce only modest improvements in the resulting dark matter annihilation constraints, typically below 20\%. Much more substantial gains are possible, however, in relatively rare realizations that contain yet-to-be-discovered satellites with large $J$-factors. These results reinforce the fact that indirect detection analyses using the population of dwarf galaxies are typically driven in large part by a small number of high-$J$-factor systems rather than by the total satellite count. We present projections for the sensitivity of Fermi-LAT and the proposed Advanced Particle-astrophysics Telescope (APT) to dark matter annihilation, finding that a complete census of the Milky Way dwarf sample could enable such instruments to probe dark matter with masses up to the TeV scale. We also investigate the dark matter discovery potential of these instruments and project their ability to measure the properties of an annihilating dark matter particle.

papers.title: Effects of dark dipole radiation on eccentric supermassive black hole binary inspirals
papers.abstract: The final-parsec problem has long posed a central challenge in understanding the merger of supermassive black hole binaries. In this paper, we investigate a scenario in which a dark scalar or vector field is sourced by eccentric binaries, leading to accelerated mergers through additional dipole radiation, and thereby extending the range of masses for which the binary can merge within a Hubble time. The Newtonian-order radiation fluxes from an eccentric charged Keplerian binary are derived using general results for localized periodic sources in flat spacetime. We find that dipole radiation, although insufficient to fully resolve the final-parsec problem, can alter the low-frequency spectrum of the stochastic gravitational wave background from supermassive black hole binary inspirals. We construct a simplified model for the spectrum and perform a Bayesian analysis using the current pulsar timing array data.

papers.title: Measuring the Angular Auto-power Spectrum of Fast Radio Burst Dispersion Measures as a Cosmological Probe and Baryon Tracer
papers.abstract: Fluctuations in the cosmic electron density are imprinted on the dispersion measures (DMs) of fast radio bursts (FRBs), making DMs a promising probe of cosmology and the spatial distribution of ionized baryons. In this work, we present the first measurement of the angular auto-power spectrum of FRB DMs, using 3455 apparently non-repeating bursts from the CHIME/FRB Catalog 2. We detect an angular correlation signal at $\sim 2.8 \sigma$ significance, associated with large-scale electron-density fluctuations. By fitting the measured spectrum to theoretical models, we constrain two key parameter combinations: $\Omega_{\rm b}h^2$-$H_0$, which probes the cosmic baryon density and expansion rate, and $\Omega_{\rm b}h^2$-$f_{\rm d}$, which traces the baryon fraction in cosmic large-scale structure (LSS). We further assess the sensitivity of the power-spectrum method to systematic uncertainties arising from the assumed FRB redshift distribution and from the DM contributions of host galaxies (${\rm DM}_{\rm host}$), the Galactic halo (${\rm DM}^{\rm MW}_{\rm halo}$), and the Milky Way interstellar medium (${\rm DM}^{\rm MW}_{\rm ISM}$), using mock samples. Our results demonstrate that the angular power spectrum is largely insensitive to uncorrelated DM components such as ${\rm DM}_{\rm host}$, thereby effectively mitigating the impact of poorly constrained host-galaxy systematics. In contrast to the mean ${\rm DM}_{\rm LSS}$-$z$ relation, this method does not require individual redshift measurements but relies only on the overall redshift distribution, and partially breaks the parameter degeneracies in the $\Omega_{\rm b}h^2$-$H_0$ and $\Omega_{\rm b}h^2$-$f_{\rm d}$ planes. These findings establish the DM angular power spectrum as a reliable cosmological probe and a powerful baryon tracer.

papers.title: XRISM Reveals a Kinematically Coherent Core System of the Nearby Cool-Core Cluster Abell 2199
papers.abstract: We present the results of a deep 251 ks XRISM/Resolve observation of the cool core of the galaxy cluster Abell 2199. From the integrated spectrum of the central $3' \times 3'$ Resolve field of view ($104 \times 104 \mathrm{~kpc}^2$), we find that the intracluster medium (ICM) redshift is consistent with that of the brightest cluster galaxy, within the optical-redshift uncertainty. This indicates that they form a kinematically coherent core system, which is offset from the mean cluster redshift by $\sim200~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}$. The observed velocity dispersion of $\sim100~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}$ corresponds to a three-dimensional Mach number of $M_{\mathrm{3D}}=0.16$ and a non-thermal pressure fraction of $P_{\mathrm{NT}}/P_{\mathrm{tot}}=1.4\pm0.2$%. Abell 2199 is one of the most dynamically quiescent relaxed clusters observed with XRISM, despite the presence of radio jets and a plume-like structure possibly associated with sloshing motions. Order-of-magnitude estimates suggest that turbulent dissipation could offset a non-negligible fraction of the radiative cooling losses, with $Q_{\mathrm{turb}}/Q_{\mathrm{cool}}\approx0.1$ for a large-scale driver such as sloshing and larger values for smaller AGN-feedback scales. Finally, we detect a localized enhancement of the Fe XXV He$\alpha$ $y$ line in the southeast region, which spatially coincides with a Chandra surface brightness discontinuity.

papers.title: Unveiling the Eigenvector 1 Sequence in BZQ Blazars. I. Mg II and Ultraviolet Fe II Emission in the UV Main Sequence
papers.abstract: We investigate the location of flat-spectrum radio quasars confirmed as blazars (BZQ-C), Fanaroff-Riley type II radio-loud (RL) quasars (FRII-Q), and radio non-detected quasars within the ultraviolet (UV) Eigenvector 1 (E1) plane defined by the Mg II line width (FWHM Mg II) and the UV Fe II strength (RFeUV). This represents the first systematic comparison of BZQ blazars with their proposed parent population in the UV E1 framework. To minimize selection biases, we construct statistically representative control subsamples and perform matched-subsample analyses in redshift and Mg II luminosity. Population differences are assessed using one- and two-dimensional non-parametric tests, including the Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Anderson-Darling, Mann-Whitney U, and Fasano-Franceschini statistics. We find that the three AGN populations occupy statistically distinct regions of the UV E1 plane. The dominant separation is driven by FWHM Mg II, with BZQ blazars systematically exhibiting narrower line profiles than FRII-Q quasars, while radio non-detected quasars lie between both populations. In contrast, RFeUV provides only limited discrimination between the RL subclasses, although it separates radio-loud from radio non-detected quasars at the population level. The observed ordering demonstrates that the UV E1 plane preserves the physical sequence expected from RL AGN unification. Inclination-dependent projection provides a natural first-order explanation for the Mg II line-width ordering. Additional differences in intrinsic BLR structure or accretion properties may contribute to the observed distributions, although the present analysis does not allow these effects to be separated independently from orientation.

papers.title: Why High-Spin Prograde MAD States Are Not Realized for AGN in Nature: Consequences for AGN Phenomenology
papers.abstract: Quasar-like and other bright active galactic nuclei are typically radio quiet despite strong evidence that many host rapidly spinning black holes. In contrast, general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations show that high-spin prograde black holes in magnetically arrested disk (MAD) states produce the most powerful relativistic jets. We show that these results are not in conflict but instead correspond to physically distinct and mutually limiting evolutionary pathways. If accretion proceeds through radiatively efficient thin disks, then as the innermost stable circular orbit decreases with increasing prograde spin, radiative output and radiation pressure rise sharply, driving strong disk winds that remove the conditions required for effective jet formation. In this branch, high-spin prograde systems are therefore expected to be jet-suppressed. Alternatively, if accretion transitions to radiatively inefficient flows capable of producing MAD states, then the spin-up to near-maximal prograde rotation proceeds on timescales that exceed the age of the universe for the relevant systems, preventing the realization of the extreme high-spin prograde MAD configurations explored in GRMHD simulations. Within this framework, powerful jets need only be produced efficiently in counterrotating systems, not maximized there, preserving the time-dependent spin evolution central to the counterrotation versus corotation paradigm of Garofalo et al. (2010). We thus reconcile GRMHD results with observations and provide a unified interpretation of the radio-loud/radio-quiet dichotomy and the cosmic evolution of powerful radio sources.

papers.title: Spectral evolution and secular shift of the Z source GX 340+0: an interpretation in the spreading layer paradigm
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive spectral and timing study of the bright neutron star low-mass X-ray binary and Z source, GX 340+0, using broadband X-ray observations with AstroSat in 2020 and 2024, focusing on the evolution of physical parameters along the Z track and the origin of secular shifts of this track across different epochs. The spectra are consistently described by the same model, comprising blackbody emission from a spreading boundary layer near the neutron star surface, an accretion disk, and a Comptonizing corona. We observe a significant decrease in the blackbody temperature from ~1.2 keV on the horizontal branch (HB) to ~1.0 keV on the normal branch (NB), which likely contributes to the harder spectra on the HB and softer spectra on the NB. At the same time, the blackbody normalization varies substantially from ~440-860, indicating changes in the effective emitting area. Within the spreading layer framework, this evolution reflects changes in the extent of theradiating layer, while the large absolute normalization values suggest an additional contribution from the boundary layer. We also detect variations in the absorption column density, suggesting structural changes in the inner accretion disk, possibly linked to radiation driven puffing-up. The Comptonized flux shows a branch-dependent behavior, remaining relatively stable along the HB but decreasing along the NB. We interpret these results within a unified framework where the boundary layer, corona, and inner disk evolve coherently with accretion rate, explaining both the Z-track behavior and its secular shifts.

papers.title: Light Shining Through the Moon: A Lunar-Occultation Helioscope for Solar Axions
papers.abstract: We propose a lunar-occultation helioscope in which the Moon suppresses the direct solar x-ray beam before solar axions enter the terrestrial magnetosphere, where they may reconvert into keV photons. We evaluate the conversion with a geomagnetic model combining the IGRF-14 internal contribution and the Tsyganenko T89 external magnetospheric contribution, retaining the two signed transverse components in the oscillation amplitude. As an explicit realizability test, we propagate a circular near-600-km polar orbit through the 12 August 2026 occultation. A $4'$-radius region around the solar center remains lunar occulted for about $470$ s while the sunward line of sight stays clear of the Earth; the coherent magnetic lever arm spans $69.1$--$96.4~\mathrm{T\,m}$ with $\mathcal I_{B,\mathrm{rms}}=76.9~\mathrm{T\,m}$. A B16-AGSS09 Primakoff calculation shows that this aperture contains $97.4\%$ of the 3--15 keV axion flux. For an explicitly specified NuSTAR-like detector benchmark, the propagated single-event exposure gives an expected low-mass 95\% C.L. sensitivity of $g_{a \gamma}=1.31\times10^{-10}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. The proposal therefore establishes the plausibility of a distinct experimental channel for solar-axion searches, characterized by a lunar-defined spatial and temporal window and by a predictable geomagnetic modulation. A future detection would additionally provide directional access to the axion-emitting solar core, opening a complementary probe of the solar interior.

papers.title: Making Reconnection Cooler: A relativistic resistive magnetohydrodynamics model for radiative collisionless reconnection
papers.abstract: Relativistic magnetic reconnection around astrophysical compact objects is a likely site for particle energization and multiwavelength emission. Kinetic theory has substantially modelled such collisionless radiative relativistic reconnection using a radiative drag force countering the acceleration of the particles. Here, we systematically derive an energy-momentum sink term in relativistic resistive magnetohydrodynamics (RRMHD), informed by kinetic theory and coupled with a charge-starved resistivity prescription which reproduces the fast reconnection rate seen in kinetic calculations, to model radiative losses. We show that our radiative loss term accurately captures important macroscopic properties -- including the temperature in the reconnection layer and the bulk motion energy distribution of the out-flowing plasma -- for inverse Compton cooling applied to two-dimensional RRMHD simulations of a reconnection layer and benchmarked to kinetic simulations. Our results hold in various cooling regimes with a one-to-one mapping to kinetic theory. Our radiative model lays a foundation for future RRMHD simulations of plasma in the relativistic radiative regime, such as in reconnection sites in a local turbulent flow or globally in the magnetospheres of black holes and neutron stars.

papers.title: Photomeson-threshold origin of the TeV break in astrophysical neutrinos: Spectrum, flavor, resolved sources, and the ultrahigh-energy landscape
papers.abstract:
IceCube observes a break near 30 TeV in the diffuse astrophysical neutrino spectrum. We interpret it as the photomeson ($p\gamma$) threshold. Accelerated protons interact with the soft x rays of accreting black holes through the $\Delta(1232)$ resonance. One kinematic relation sets the break energy from the target field's lowest photon energy, the seed scale $\varepsilon_0$. The measured break fixes $\varepsilon_0\simeq0.13$ keV and supplies the low-energy suppression no sum of falling power laws can produce. Building on the $\Delta(1232)$ identification of Khatee Zathul, Fang, Halzen, and Hooper and the single-source-class photo-pion fit of Winter, Fiorillo, and Buson, we give closed-form relations that invert the four broken-power-law parameters to the source physics with no remaining freedom, namely, $\gamma_2=s$ and $\gamma_1=s-(\alpha_x-1)$ ($s$, $\alpha_x$ the proton and target photon indices), and $E_{m br}\propto[(1+ ar z)\varepsilon_0]^{-1}$. The break width bounds the total smearing to $\sigma_s\le0.235$ dex (68% CL), no broader than redshift alone must make it, and the seed scale is the same across sources to within a factor $\lesssim$1.5, which mean-spectrum fits do not provide. Below-break neutrinos are predicted to come on average from higher redshifts than those above. The threshold also fixes the flavor and $
u/ ar
u$ composition, including the energy-dependent $ ar
u_e$ fraction and the Glashow-resonance discriminator of Winter et al., matching current flavor data. Inverted source by source, the relation gives each resolved IceCube source its target photon scale, from the keV coronae of NGC 1068 and PKS 1424+240 to the $\sim$20 eV jet of TXS 0506+056. That two-decade spread means they cannot supply the homogeneous break, which requires a separate, fainter population. KM3-230213A points to a warm-dust target, $\varepsilon_0\simeq0.02$ eV, unless cosmogenic.

papers.title: On the Sensitivity of Fermi-LAT Maximum Likelihood Stacking
papers.abstract: Stacking sub-threshold gamma-ray sources has become common practice for understanding high-energy emission processes at the population level. In this procedure, one co-adds log-likelihood ratios, called TS values (TS = 2ln$(L_1/L_0)$), for a source class of interest. It is best practice to compare the population of sub-threshold targets against a population of control field test sources (CFs) selected to represent the unmodeled \gray\ background. Determining the significance of a TS measurement stack has typically been difficult. In this work, we find the necessary cumulative TS value ($\Sigma$TS) of a sub-threshold population of $N$ targets to achieve a $5\sigma$ separation from a like-sized population of CFs. We find that the $\Delta (\Sigma$TS) needed to achieve a $5\sigma$ separation is $\sim 70$. In taking this measurement, we characterize the source distribution corresponding to the measured $\Sigma$TS for a significantly detected stack and even predict new individual source detections in larger stacks.

papers.title: Early Evolution of Strange Quark Stars Admixed with Fermionic Dark Matter
papers.abstract: We study strange quark stars admixed with fermionic dark matter (DM) in three quasistatic stages of their early evolution: the neutrino-trapped stage, the heated stage after deleptonization, and the cold stage. Quark matter is described by the MIT bag model at finite temperature with thermal gluons, a repulsive vector interaction, and, in the first stage, trapped neutrinos. The DM is modeled as a cold, asymmetric gas of fermions with masses $m_\chi = 0.3$, $1$, and $3$ GeV, with and without a repulsive self-interaction, and interacts with the quark matter only through gravity. Using the two-fluid Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations, we compute the structure, the maximum masses, and the tidal deformability of the stars in each stage for DM mass fractions $F_D$ up to $5\%$, and we follow individual stars at fixed numbers of baryons and DM particles. The effect of DM is nearly the same in the three stages: for $m_\chi = 1$ GeV and $F_D = 5\%$, DM lowers the maximum mass by about $8\%$ and the tidal deformability of a $1.4\,M_\odot$ star by about $26\%$ in each stage, whereas the stage itself changes these quantities by only a few percent. Heavy DM forms a compact core; for $m_\chi = 3$ GeV without self-interaction, the mass limit of this core can set the maximum mass of the star. Light DM can form an extended halo, which does not increase the maximum mass for the fractions considered. For $m_\chi = 1$ GeV and $F_D = 5\%$, DM lowers the largest baryon mass of a newborn star by about $0.23\,M_\odot$, but this limit increases from the neutrino-trapped to the cold stage in all cases considered, so that DM does not cause a delayed collapse to a black hole. In our model, pulsars of about $2\,M_\odot$ require a stiff quark equation of state and restrict the DM fraction to a few percent unless the DM is light.

papers.title: Tearing stability of pulsar equatorial current sheets
papers.abstract: Harris-type current sheets have been studied extensively with particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. These local configurations generally contain no systematic magnetic-field component normal to the current sheet. Such a component develops naturally in a global pulsar magnetosphere because reconnecting field lines connect the northern and southern magnetic hemispheres. We investigate how the normal field component affects the tearing stability and dissipation of the pulsar equatorial current sheet, and we examine the consequences for the global magnetospheric configuration. We combine the tearing-stability condition for a current sheet threaded by a normal field with the electromagnetic relations imposed by the surrounding ideal force-free magnetosphere. We also formulate a dissipative equatorial boundary condition and incorporate it into a global force-free model solved with physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). For realistic Lundquist numbers the normal magnetic field can suppress the tearing instability. Preliminary solutions indicate two distinct magnetospheric configurations: a nearly ideal CKF-like state with negligible equatorial dissipation, and a strongly dissipative state resembling the solutions of Contopoulos et al. (2014) and Cerutti et al. (2015). The reconnection rate in the pulsar equatorial current sheet cannot be inferred from local Harris-type current sheet calculations because it depends on the global magnetic topology. Present global 3D PIC simulations operate at effective Lundquist numbers far below astrophysical values, and may therefore exhibit tearing that in a real pulsar magnetosphere would be strongly suppressed.

papers.title: Probabilistic foreground diagnostics from dispersion measure excess in individual fast radio bursts
papers.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) provide a unique probe of diffuse baryons through their dispersion measure (DM), but interpreting a large DM for an individual burst is limited by the uncertain contribution from its host galaxy, which is hard to directly observed. We address this gap with a source-level diagnostic framework that treats $\mathrm{DM_{host}}$ as a latent variable drawn from a shared lognormal population, thereby marginalizing over the uncertain host contribution. Applying an expectation--maximization (EM) inference scheme to 92 localized FRBs, we jointly estimate the host-DM population and obtain a model-conditioned host-DM distribution for each burst. We propagate these distributions into an excess cosmological DM for each sightline, quantifying both its uncertainty and the probability that a positive excess remains after accounting for the host contribution. FRBs previously reported to show evidence for foreground or intervening contributions preferentially exhibit high probabilities of retaining such an excess, indicating that this source-level probability can provide a useful statistic for prioritizing foreground follow-up observations. Using this diagnostic, we identify 18 additional localized FRBs as high-priority candidates for follow-up searches for possible intervening galaxies, groups, clusters, or large-scale structure.

papers.title: Probing Accretion Disk Dynamics of GS 1354-64: Insights from 2025$-$2026 Complex Outburst
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive spectro-temporal study of the 2025--2026 outburst of the Galactic black hole X-ray binary GS 1354$-$64 using observations from MAXI/GSC, Insight-HXMT, and NuSTAR. The source underwent a $\sim126$ day outburst characterized by an `unusual' sequence of spectral states driven by three short X-ray flares ($\sim2$, 5, and 7~days), likely triggered by episodic enhancements in the Keplerian flow. These flares produced rapid spectral softening and delayed the outburst decay. The MAXI/GSC light curves show soft X-ray dominance during the intermediate $\sim90$ days of the outburst. Corresponding minima in the hardness ratio and forward-to-backward loops in the hardness--intensity diagram indicate repeated spectral softening and episodic changes in the accretion flow. Low-frequency type-C QPOs exhibit a three-phase evolution, with frequencies increasing from $0.07$ to $5.76$~Hz, decreasing from $6.14$ to $3.26$~Hz, and rising again to $6.25$~Hz with a sporadic detection of type-B QPOs in the intermediate state. The propagating oscillatory shock model successfully reproduces this evolution through inward shock propagation during the rising phase, followed by rapid outward and gradual inward motion during plateau-1, tracing changes in the Comptonizing corona. Broadband ($2-70$~keV) spectral analysis reveals coupled evolution of the thermal (diskbb: $T_{\rm in}=0.25$--$1.04$~keV) and Comptonized (thcomp: $\Gamma_{\rm th}=1.69$--$2.66$, $f_{\rm cov}\sim0.02$--$0.97$) components. Relativistic reflection is well described by the relline model, while an additional powerlaw above $\sim50$~keV in the initial hard state suggests a high-energy component, possibly associated with synchrotron cooling. Strong correlations between QPO frequency, photon index, and hardness ratio constrain the evolution of the accretion flow geometry and Comptonizing corona.

papers.title: Long-Term Evolution of Hills-Captured Stars with TDE Disk Collisions: Links to Repeating Nuclear Transients
papers.abstract: Quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs) and repeating partial tidal disruption event (rpTDE) candidates are widely interpreted as being powered by a star on an hours-to-years orbit around a massive black hole (MBH). Every such orbiter model presupposes a star delivered onto an extraordinarily compact orbit without being destroyed, but it is unclear whether this is achievable. We follow the coupled orbital and stellar evolution of stars captured by the Hills mechanism, combining gas drag and per-collision mass loss from recurrent TDE disks with gravitational-wave (GW) orbital decay and stochastic two-body relaxation in a Monte Carlo model. Conventionally, the EMRI-formation criterion is based on comparing the timescales of GW decay and orbital angular momentum relaxation. We find that this criterion severely overestimates the EMRI rate: for relaxation timescales shorter than a Hubble time, most Hills-captured stars are tidally disrupted before GW emission can circularize the stellar orbit. Instead, TDE-disk drag plays a crucial role in the orbital evolution and can boost the fraction of stars reaching QPE orbits by an order of magnitude or more, assuming that the disk aspect ratio is relatively large $H/r \sim 0.1$. We also find that collisional ablation imposes a minimum orbital period that rises with MBH mass and precludes sub-day orbits for $M_{\rm BH} \gtrsim 10^6\,M_\odot$, unless GWs alone can drive orbital decay faster than orbital relaxation. This can explain the observed preference of short-period QPEs for low-mass MBHs. Most known rpTDEs lie below the Hills-capture period minimum and thus require additional orbital decay, which TDE-disk drag can plausibly supply. These results support the viability of the orbiter model; our predictions of the MBH mass and orbital period distributions can be used to further test this model.

papers.title: Scintillation arcs for fast pulsar binaries: the Double Pulsar
papers.abstract: The double pulsar PSR J0737-3039A is a prime system for tests of gravity. A precise distance would strengthen these tests and also open up the possibility to measure the fast pulsar's moment of inertia, allowing a direct constraint on the equation of state of ultra-dense matter. Current parallax estimates from pulsar timing and very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) are in tension, which motivates complementary constraints. Information about distances is encoded in pulsar scintillation, but a complication for the double pulsar is that rapid orbital motion makes the interpretation difficult. We introduce an orbital motion ``resampling'' technique to overcome this complication, and use it to determine the properties of the principal scattering screen and the pulsar binary. Our fits yield a pulsar distance, of $781^{+62}_{-94}{\rm\,pc}$, in better agreement with the VLBI-based distance, but find that the nearly edge-on orbit precludes a precise measurement. For the principal screen, we infer a distance of $270^{+24}_{-23}{\rm\,pc}$, an orientation of $73.1^{\circ}\pm2.6^{\circ}$ E of N, and a transverse speed of $-15.2\pm1.0{\rm\,km/s}$. We also demonstrate the presence of a second screen, whose properties we can only partially determine: it is oriented roughly perpendicularly to the first screen and at a larger distance, of $\gtrsim\!547{\rm\,pc}$. To benchmark our technique and its uncertainties, we develop simulations of the system, generating artificial data that match the characteristics of the observed ones. We also discuss how future improvements to the method and use of the second screen could enable a more precise distance measurement.

papers.title: Dual Horizon-MAD: A New Mode of Binary Black Hole Magnetically Arrested Accretion with Saturated Horizon Magnetic Fluxes and Intermittent Minidisks
papers.abstract: Reliable first-principles predictions of multimessenger signals from inspiralling supermassive binary black holes (SMBBHs) require magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations in full general relativity (GR) that resolve the accretion flow down to the black hole horizons. However, performing such simulations long enough to relax the magnetohydrodynamics near the BBHs is computationally challenging and a source of uncertainty in modeling efforts. In this work, we present the longest MHD simulation of circumbinary disk (CBD) accretion onto a SMBBH in full GR. The equal-mass, quasicircular, nonspining BBH starts at an initial separation of $d/M=30$ and evolves over $\sim56$ orbits ($t \simeq 52,000 \, GM/c^3$), relaxing the magnetic field dynamics within the CBD cavity. After $\sim 23$ orbits and persistent magnetically arrested minidisks, the accretion enters a new magnetically arrested mode which we call dual horizon-MAD (DH-MAD). In DH-MAD, the dimensionless horizon magnetic fluxes remain saturated at $\phi_{BH}\sim 20$ driving magnetic flux eruptions from the vicinity of the BH horizons, and the vertical magnetic flux in the cavity saturates, but no flux eruptions occur at the cavity-CBD boundary. During this DH-MAD phase, there is also a shift in the total mass accretion rate variability, which exhibits a periodicity of $f\sim 1.8 f_{\rm orb}$, while the accretion rate modulation on the individual black holes occurs almost at the orbital period, $f\sim 0.9 f_{\rm orb}$. $\phi_{BH}$ also exhibits a robust periodicity at $f\sim 0.4 f_{\rm orb}$, suggesting that quasiperiodic nonthermal emission from magnetic reconnection near the horizons could be a smoking gun electromagnetic counterpart to inspiraling SMBBHs. Finally, minidisks around the BHs become intermittent in the DH-MAD phase, even at a separation of $d/M = 24$, likely due to the large plasma magnetization in the optically thin cavity.

papers.title: Fast Radio Bursts Co-detected by CHIME/FRB and DSA-110 from 400 to 1530 MHz
papers.abstract: We present a sample of $15$ fast radio bursts (FRBs) that were co-detected by the Deep Synoptic Array (DSA-110) and the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME) between 2022 and 2024, of which $12$ have channelized voltage data from both instruments and 9 have secure redshifts. All but one are as-yet-non-repeating. Most bursts span the entire bandwidth of each instrument (400-800 MHz for CHIME, 1280-1530 MHz for DSA-110), significantly expanding the number of FRBs known to emit across $>1$ GHz of spectral bandwidth and constraining the spectral evolution of energy and propagation effects. On average, the FRBs exhibit higher spectral energies (up to a factor of $\sim10$) in the CHIME band but are lower in peak flux density due to substantial pulse broadening. The sample mean (median) spectral index $-0.4\pm0.4$ ($-0.3\pm0.4$) is shallower than previously reported spectral indices, likely a selection effect. A third of the sample shows evidence for a spectral turnover, comparable to that seen in GHz-peaked pulsar and magnetar spectra. Joint scintillation and pulse broadening constraints indicate that nearly all bursts encounter multiple scattering screens, with pulse broadening originating within their host galaxies. The co-detected bursts are among the most scattered in the CHIME/FRB sample, while being the narrowest in the DSA-110 sample, indicating that CHIME/FRB and DSA-110 select different subsets of the FRB population; the interplay between intrinsic burst width, scattering, and the FRB search time resolution creates a narrow window of sensitivity to co-detected FRBs, providing a blueprint for future ultra-wideband FRB surveys.

papers.title: Spectropolarimetric properties of fast radio bursts co-detected by CHIME/FRB and DSA-110
papers.abstract: We present spectropolarimetric analysis of twelve fast radio bursts (FRBs) co-detected by CHIME/FRB and DSA-110, eleven of which are apparently non-repeating. We obtain broadband spectral coverage (400-1530 MHz) for these FRBs and constrain propagation effects in their polarized spectra. We observe two notable spectral features: (i) in three FRBs, we find decreasing linear polarization fraction with increasing frequency and, (ii) in seven FRBs, we find that the linear polarization fraction decreases with decreasing frequency. The former spectral signature is commonly observed in radio pulsars and is suggestive of magnetospheric emission, where either the mixing of orthogonally polarized modes or incoherent summing of unresolved burst components may cause depolarization at high frequencies. The latter is consistent with depolarization due to multipath propagation. We report the first statistically significant correlation (3.5-3.9$\sigma$) between the extent of depolarization and amplitude of Faraday rotation arising from FRB host galaxies, implying that the two effects likely arise in the same turbulent, magnetoionic environments around FRB sources. The prevalence of depolarization in our sample suggests that turbulent environments that have, thus far, been predominantly associated with some repeating FRBs, may also be commonly present around a subset of apparently non-repeating FRBs. We highlight a systematic bias for detecting a disproportionately high fraction of constant polarization angle (PA) profiles in low-frequency FRB surveys due to amplified scatter broadening, which we also observe in two of our co-detected FRBs.

papers.title: The FRB Population Revisited: Rate, Energy, Evolution, and Host-DM Constraints from the Second CHIME/FRB Catalog
papers.abstract: We present a study that simultaneously fits for key fast radio burst (FRB) population properties using the Second CHIME/FRB Catalog while calibrating for instrumental selection effects. Our inferred volumetric rate at $z=0$ is $1.1^{+0.4}_{-0.3}\times 10^{5}\,{\rm Gpc}^{-3}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$ above an isotropic-equivalent energy of $10^{39}$ erg and below a scattering timescale of 30 ms at 600 MHz. The evolution of the FRB rate relative to the cosmic star formation rate remains statistically unconstrained. Assuming a Schechter function for the energy distribution, isotropic emission, and 1-GHz emission bandwidth, we find a characteristic maximum energy of $2.0^{+2.6}_{-1.0} \times 10^{41}$ erg and a differential power-law index of $-1.41\,^{+0.27}_{-0.21}({\rm stat.})\,\pm\,0.35({\rm sys.})$. The host galaxy contribution to the observed dispersion measure (DM) is modeled as a log-normal distribution; assuming a total Galactic contribution of 80 $\text{pc cm}^{-3}$, we find a median host-galaxy DM contribution of $199^{+34}_{-36}\;\text{pc cm}^{-3}$ in the rest-frame. Finally, we find that the average FRB spectrum, described by a spectral index of $\alpha=-1.0^{+0.5}_{-0.6}$, is inconsistent with being flat at the $\sim2\sigma$ level. We note an excess of high-S/N bursts at low DMs in the observed sample that is not predicted by the best-fit model. Testing alternative models does not alleviate this tension; future population studies may mitigate this limitation by incorporating robust fluence and redshift measurements.

papers.title: Modeling extraordinary relativistic jets on the scale of the cosmic web
papers.abstract: Recent observations of supermassive black hole jets extending up to the typical sizes of cosmic web filaments challenge our current understanding. In particular, the overall jet size of J152932.16+601534.4 ("Porphyrion") reaches $\sim 7$ Mpc at redshift 0.896. Magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) models of relativistic jets have never been successfully applied to such extraordinary distances, requiring demanding jet-environment and flow stability conditions. By using state-of-the-art numerical simulations of 3D relativistic-MHD jets, we show that Porphyrion's observational properties can be successfully modelled in a realistic scenario, involving a jet kinetic power of $3.5 \times 10^{46}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and an external medium of a low-density galaxy group. We find that the pair of jets expands to $\sim 9$ Mpc in about $20$ Myr, implying that the jet grows with relativistic speeds for most of its evolution. Comparing this case with other jets of similar power propagating in substantially denser cosmic structures, we find much slower outflows that can only reach a few Mpc, consistent with the bulk of the observed population of giant radio galaxies. Our results make a testable prediction, i.e. future detections of even larger-scale jets in upcoming surveys and database searches will be invaluable in studying the demographics and feedback of the poorly known population of powerful jets, particularly in under-dense regions of the cosmic web.

papers.title: The Most X-ray Luminous Fast Blue Optical Transient at Early Times: AT 2024qfm and Inefficient Reprocessing of Its High-Energy Emission
papers.abstract: We present comprehensive multiwavelength (X-ray, UV, optical, and radio) observations of the Luminous Fast Blue Optical Transient (LFBOT) AT 2024qfm. At $z = 0.227$ and reaching $L_{\rm x}\approx 10^{44}\,\rm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, AT 2024qfm is the most X-ray luminous LFBOT at $\delta t < 20$ days, and the least luminous at mm wavelengths. The X-ray emission shows a rapid ($\propto t^{-6}$) decay in the first $\approx 6$ days followed by a brightening at $\delta t \approx 15$ days that is accompanied by significant spectral hardening. Similarly to other LFBOTs, optical spectra remain featureless, and the UV-optical emission is dominated by a hot thermal continuum with temperature $T> 10000$ K until $\delta t \approx 14$ days. AT 2024qfm shows luminous radio emission that is broadly consistent with the interaction of a fast ($\Gamma \beta c \approx 0.2$ c) shock wave with a dense medium ($n_{\rm CSM} \approx 6 \times 10^{4}\, \rm cm^{-3}$ at $R \approx 1.3 \times 10^{16}$ cm). Interestingly, the radio spectra do not evolve between $\delta t \approx 40-58$ days, indicating multiple outflow components shocking the surrounding medium. Peculiar to AT2024qfm is that this LFBOT reaches $L_{\rm x} \approx L_{\rm opt}$ at much earlier times ($\delta t \approx 7$ days) than observed for AT 2018cow and AT 2024wpp, suggesting less efficient re-processing of X-rays. Finally, a compilation of the X-ray spectral properties of all known LFBOTs shows that they consistently exhibit harder X-ray spectra than GRB afterglows, indicating a different emission mechanism and/or regimes between the two source classes.

papers.title: Constraining Planet Nine with Pulsar Timing: Orbit Determination Method from the Acceleration, Jerk, and Snap of the Solar System Barycenter
papers.abstract: Planet Nine is hypothesized to exist in the outer solar system in order to explain the physical orbital clustering of several trans-Neptunian objects. A Planet Nine would systematically change the location of the solar system barycenter (SSB). Therefore, the precise timing properties of millisecond radio pulsars would measure the acceleration, jerk, and snap of the currently-perceived SSB under the gravitational influence of a Planet Nine. We present a method on how to use pulsar spin frequency derivatives and binary pulsar orbital period derivatives to constrain the Planet Nine parameter space. We find that searches for unidentified massive objects in the solar system require at least cubic and quartic variations in the pulse times of arrival (corresponding to jerk and snap, respectively) in order to uniquely constrain an orbit. Otherwise, additional assumptions are required to fully constrain the mass and orbital parameters of the object. We use our method to weigh the ice giants Uranus and Neptune and obtain results consistent with the literature. This method could be used to weigh a Planet Nine after a putative optical detection. Future work will use updated pulsar timing datasets that benefit from longer observational baselines and advances in statistical modeling and noise characterization.

papers.title: Time-variable tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems
papers.abstract: Most stars in the field are part of binary, triple, or higher-order systems, which we primarily observe in hierarchical configurations that allow long-term stability. Over long timescales, hierarchical triple systems interact primarily through gravitational dynamics, but more complex interactions arise when stellar evolution drives mass transfer. In this paper, we study tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems using three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations. We find that the finite separation of the inner binary produces oscillations in the Roche potential that critically alter both the donor star's variability and its mean mass-loss rate. For compact inner binaries, the mass-loss rate approaches that of a single accretor, while at larger separations the orbit-averaged mass-loss rate increases steeply, approximately as $\langle \dot{M}_d\rangle \propto \langle \dot{M}_{d,0}\rangle (1+C a_b^{6.1 \pm 0.9})$. For the $\gamma = 5/3$ polytropic donor considered here, this scaling is consistent with the nonlinear response of Roche-lobe overflow to the leading quadrupolar perturbation of the inner-binary potential, which scales as $\delta\Phi_2 \propto a_b^2$. We also examine the donor's response to periodic forcing from the inner binary and find a transition between individual and collaborative accretion that determines whether the transferred material can form and sustain a circumbinary disk. Our results show that the finite separation of the inner binary can strongly regulate both the rate and fate of tertiary mass transfer, constraining a poorly understood phase of hierarchical triple evolution.

papers.title: Sound of Keplerian binaries in a homogeneous Newtonian fluid background
papers.abstract: We formulate the dissipation due to sound-wave emission from a Keplerian binary embedded in a homogeneous Newtonian fluid background at rest in the binary center-of-mass frame within linear perturbation theory. Rather than starting from the local wake force, we treat the binary as a localized periodic mass source and compute the sound-wave fluxes carried away by the medium. The time-averaged energy, linear-momentum, and angular-momentum fluxes are obtained from Noether currents of the fluid perturbations. For a classical inviscid barotropic Newtonian fluid, retaining the self-gravity of density perturbations while adopting the Jeans prescription, we derive explicit flux formulas for circular and eccentric binaries with arbitrary mass ratio. This formulation also clarifies the ultraviolet behavior of point sources: in a nondispersive fluid, the harmonic sum becomes cutoff-sensitive precisely when at least one component becomes supersonic. We examine explicitly how finite source size removes this divergence using a uniform-sphere model and relate the resulting regularization to a corresponding effective harmonic cutoff. The associated secular eccentricity evolution exhibits circularization in the subsonic regime when the fluid self-gravity is sufficiently weak but can change sign outside this regime, with eccentricity growth in the strictly supersonic UV limit. For a Schr\"odinger-Poisson quantum fluid, quantum pressure instead softens the high-frequency contribution and renders the point-source fluxes UV finite within the nonrelativistic regime; our numerical results further indicate eccentricity growth due to sound radiation over the parameter space explored. Finally, we translate orbital-decay measurements of two binary pulsars into order-of-magnitude bounds on the homogeneous quantum-fluid density surrounding each system.

papers.title: On extracting Science information from a large data set of RXTE X-ray binary spectra using KDE technique
papers.abstract: Machine Learning/Neural Networks have been successively and extensively used in Astronomy (and other subjects) for class identification of objects based on large data sets. However, it remains difficult to extract other science information, such as what the characteristics of the class are that allow for definite identification, and whether there are objects in the sample that are unique and hence of possible science interest. An alternate approach based on rank ordering of variables and Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) may be used for class identification and to infer such science information. We test the method on a previously analyzed data set of RXTE spectra of low-mass X-ray binaries and find that black hole and neutron star systems can be distinguished at an accuracy level of ~93%, which is comparable to deep learning techniques. The soft state spectra of black hole systems are distinct from neutron star ones. For the whole sample, observations of the pulsar 4U 1907+097 (which was inadvertently introduced into the data set) were clearly found to be unique. The previously reported hyper-soft states of GRO J1655-40 and XTE J1550-564 are found to be unique among black hole spectra. For the rest of the neutron stars, the method identifies some unreported spectra of EXO 1745-248 as unique because they seem to be relativistic reflection-dominated spectra. We discuss the potential and scalability of this method.
